A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scalable GANs with Transformers and retain identifiable corresponding methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-256 generation results, model-scaling experiments, component ablations, representation analyses, and generated examples in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original GAT experiments and adds results for higher-resolution generation, MS-COCO text-to-image generation, unconditional FFHQ generation, editing, and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The core GAT architecture, MNG procedure, width-aware learning-rate rule, and loss formulations remain. Appendix A.8 adds a localized MM-GAT adaptation: frozen CLIP word tokens enter through MM-DiT-style conditioning, while the sentence embedding supplies global conditioning. This changes the model's inputs and conditioning beyond merely testing it on another dataset.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional ImageNet-256 generation and latent interpolation. v2 adds ImageNet-512 generation, MS-COCO text-to-image generation, unconditional FFHQ-256 generation, and unsupervised and text-directed image editing using GANSpace and StyleCLIP. These substantially broaden the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds STARFlow and LightningDiT-XL/2 to the retained ImageNet comparisons. The new MS-COCO comparison in Table 8 introduces a substantial additional comparator set, including Frido, VQ-Diffusion, U-ViT variants, AttnGAN, DM-GAN, DF-GAN, XMC-GAN, and LAFITE.

E3.justification: The headline training budget increases from 40 to 60 epochs, with v2 A.1 setting the gradient-penalty coefficient to 10 for epochs 40–60 after the original 0.1 setting. Existing patch-size and ablation plots switch from FID-5K to FID-50K. v2 also introduces CLIP-FID, precision/recall, latency/memory evaluation, and a fourfold-batch-size experiment with doubled learning rate.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PCA, block-removal, and component ablations, v2 tests early-layer input/output similarity and sensitivity to latent noise, compatibility with larger batches, alternative tokenizers, and seed variation. It also adds REPA ablation at another model size, removal of REPA during continued training, and a training-compute scaling fit. These address additional mechanism and robustness questions.

E5.justification: v1 does not report a seed-replication analysis. v2 A.16 reports individual FID-5K outcomes from three differently seeded, 10-epoch GAT-S/2 runs alongside the original result. This provides limited seed-sensitivity evidence, without confidence intervals or systematic uncertainty reporting for the main comparisons.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports 40-epoch FID 3.02 without guidance and 2.96 with guidance; v2 reports 2.18 at 60 epochs under a revised training schedule, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Original 20-epoch capacity scores remain in v2 Table 5. Substantial new results include ImageNet-512 FID 4.04, MS-COCO FID 7.98, FFHQ FID 9.74, and additional diversity, resource, and robustness measurements.

T1.justification: v1 states the inverse-width learning-rate rule and its rationale. v2 A.10 adds explicit independent, unit-variance channel assumptions, a definition of functional update magnitude, and a linear-layer SGD derivation relating output changes to learning rate times width. This is limited mathematical support, explicitly presented without a full proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains scalable latent-space transformer GANs using MNG and width-aware learning rates. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion revise the quantified headline from FID 2.96 in 40 epochs with sixfold fewer epochs to FID 2.18 in 60 epochs with fourfold fewer epochs. The main contribution is retained while its performance and efficiency claim changes.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of early-layer underuse through final-output-only supervision, interprets deterioration after removing REPA as discriminator feature erosion, and discusses training-cost tradeoffs. Appendices A.8, A.10–A.11, and A.16 qualify the preliminary text-conditioning extension, simplified mathematical argument, depth/batch generalization, and limited seed coverage. These substantially expand interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, MM-GAT configuration details, alternative-tokenizer specifications, compute-accounting procedures, GPU benchmarking settings, and REPA overhead measurements. Training-resource disclosure is updated for the longer run. However, it removes v1 A.1's precise guidance recipe—strength 1.1 applied to the first 30% of blocks—and no longer clearly distinguishes guided and unguided headline results.

R1.justification: Literature coverage expands substantially into text-conditioned generation, latent editing, gradient normalization, and batch-size scaling, with new references including CLIP, GANSpace, StyleCLIP, and STARFlow. v2 also drops the explicit first-time claim in Section 2.2 and the connection to equalized learning rates and Karras et al. (2017). Publication updates and duplicate entries for existing works do not constitute additional research.

P1.justification: v2 substantially edits the abstract, introductory and architectural explanations, experimental setup, and early-layer discussion. It separates early-layer diagnosis from component ablations, reorganizes the further-analysis narrative, and restructures the appendix into topical sections. These changes extend beyond inserting new experimental results.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column main paper with revised table and caption formatting. Figure 3 gains a training-compute panel, ablation axes are redrawn, and numerous task, metric, cost, and editing displays are added. Existing material is also relocated or condensed: v1 Tables 2–3 become v2 Tables 4–5, and v1 Figure 8 becomes v2 Figure 12; some older sample galleries are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's ImageNet-256-centered evidence. Additional generation tasks, CLIP-FID and diversity metrics, targeted mechanism and robustness tests, and resource measurements better support generality and efficiency claims. The improved headline FID uses longer training and a changed penalty, so it is not decisive by itself. Lost guidance details and the incorrect MNG labeling of the learning-rate ablation in Table 6 weaken reproducibility, but the broader, more diagnostic evidence provides a clear substantial net improvement.
